'''Arts and culture'''
*[[France–Mexico relations]]

Mexico continues seeking the [[codex]]'s permanent [[Repatriation (cultural property)|return]] from France. '''Health and environment'''
*[[Environmental policy of the second Trump administration]]
**The [[United States Fish and Wildlife Service]] narrows its enforcement of the [[Endangered Species Act of 1973|Endangered Species Act]] by excluding unintentional [[Fauna of the United States|wildlife]] deaths from its definition of prohibited [[Take (hunting)|take]], including foreseeable deaths linked to activities such as [[Fishing industry in the United States|commercial fishing]] and [[History of the lumber industry in the United States|logging]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260917-trump-admin-overhauls-key-protection-for-endangered-species (AFP via France 24)]
*Biologists publish a study in the journal ''[[Current Biology]]'' describing a new species of [[Wildcat|wild cat]] belonging to the genus ''[[Leopardus]]'', commonly called the "[[Tilcayo tiger cat|tilcayo]]", in the [[Bolivian Yungas|Yungas]] [[cloud forest]]s of [[Bolivia]]. This discovery marks the first new cat species in over 100 years. [https://www.doi.org/10.1016/j.cub.2026.08.059  (''Cell'')] [https://www.reuters.com/business/environment/new-cat-species-identified-bolivia-first-over-century-2026-09-17/ (Reuters)]
*The [[National Institute for Health and Care Excellence]] approves the [[Trastuzumab deruxtecan]] drug for women in [[England]] with [[Metastatic breast cancer|metastatic]] or incurable [[HER2]]-[[breast cancer]] that cannot be removed surgically, making it the first licensed targeted treatment for patients, two years after it was rejected due to its cost effectiveness. [https://news.sky.com/story/life-extending-drug-for-breast-cancer-patients-now-on-nhs-in-england-13588795 (Sky News)] [https://www.independent.co.uk/news/uk/home-news/enhertu-breast-cancer-life-extending-drug-b3051691.html (''The Independent'')]

'''International relations'''
*[[Eighty-First session of the United Nations General Assembly]], [[Palestine and the United Nations]]
**The [[United Nations General Assembly]] (UNGA) votes 152–3, with four abstentions, to allow [[President of Palestine|Palestinian president]] [[Mahmoud Abbas]] and other senior [[Government of Palestine|Palestinian officials]] to address [[United Nations|UN]] meetings, including the [[General debate of the eighty-first session of the United Nations General Assembly|general debate]] of the eighty-first session of the UNGA, by video for one year after [[Visa policy of the United States|United States visa]] restrictions prevented their travel to [[New York City]], where the [[UN headquarters]] are. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/un-allows-palestinian-president-again-speak-via-video-after-us-denies-visa-2026-09-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Israel–Serbia relations]]
**[[Serbian president]] [[Aleksandar Vučić]] inaugurates a factory for [[Israel|Israeli]]-made [[Military drone|drones]] that will be produced by [[Serbia|the country]]'s [[Krušik (company)|Krušik]] company, with Vučić stating that it will employ 100 people and produce advanced equipment for the [[Serbian military]]. [https://apnews.com/article/serbia-israel-drones-factory-vucic-military-12098645a942e8fef5b58911e37e9fb2 (AP)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Human rights in Pakistan]]
**[[Pakistan]]'s [[Supreme Court of Pakistan|Supreme Court]] suspends 17-year [[Prisons in Pakistan|prison]] sentences imposed on human rights lawyer [[Imaan Mazari]] and her husband over [[Anti-Pakistan sentiment|anti-state]] [[social media]] posts, and grants them [[bail]] pending an [[Islamabad High Court]] ruling. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistans-top-court-suspends-sentences-rights-lawyer-mazari-husband-2026-09-17/ (Reuters)]
*[[Malawi Police Service|Malawian police]] rescue a 47-year-old [[British diaspora in Africa|British]] woman after her abduction in [[Blantyre]]. Four suspected kidnappers are killed in a [[shootout]] with officers, while a senior police officer is injured and hospitalized in stable condition. [https://abcnews.com/International/wireStory/4-suspects-killed-shootout-police-rescue-kidnapped-british-136551217 (AP via ABC News)]
*Thirty-seven suspected [[Illegal mining|illegal]] [[Mining industry of Nigeria|gold miners]] die in custody of [[Nigeria]]'s [[Nigeria Security and Civil Defence Corps|civil defence agency]] in [[Minna]], [[Niger State]]. Survivors say [[overcrowding]] and poor ventilation caused breathing difficulties, while an [[National Intelligence Agency (Nigeria)|intelligence]] report links the deaths to those conditions. The government orders an investigation. [https://www.afp.com/en/nigeria-miners-struggled-breathe-cell-37-died-survivors (AFP)]

* [[2026 Swedish general election]]
** [[Ulf Kristersson]] announces his resignation as [[Prime Minister of Sweden]] after his [[Conservatism in Sweden|right-wing]] bloc wins 173 seats in the [[Riksdag]], compared to 176 won by the opposition, led by [[Magdalena Andersson]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/9/17/sweden-prime-minister-to-resign-as-left-wing-bloc-seals-narrow-election-win (Al Jazeera)] [https://www.bbc.com/news/articles/cxr50l3d762po (BBC News)]
*[[Censorship and media control during the Venezuelan presidential crisis]]
**[[Venezuela]] restores access to 17 [[Mass media in Venezuela|news websites]] that were previously [[Censorship in Venezuela|blocked]], including [[EFE]], ''[[El Nacional (Venezuela)|El Nacional]]'', [[NTN24]], and ''[[Semana]]'', as [[Interim government of Delcy Rodríguez|the interim government]] and [[Venezuelan opposition|opposition]] resume [[Negotiations during the Venezuelan crisis|political transition talks]] that include [[Human rights in Venezuela#Press freedom|freedom of expression]]. [https://gulfnews.com/world/americas/venezuela-unblocks-some-censored-news-sites-2-1.500678849 (AFP via ''Gulf News'')]
*[[Visa policy of Australia]]
**[[Australia]] tightens visa rules for [[International students in Australia|international students]] and [[Working holidays in Australia|working holidaymakers]], restricts visa switching, and increases enforcement against [[Illegal immigration to Australia|overstayers]] as it seeks to reduce [[Immigration to Australia|net overseas migration]] to 225,000 by 2027–28 and ease [[Australian property bubble|pressure on housing]]. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20260917-australia-to-cut-migration-to-fix-housing-crisis-minister (AFP via France 24)]
